correctness.rationale: Commuting moduli have a simultaneous eigenbasis. Jensen--Schur--Horn and columnwise triangle bound prove the coefficient one through p=2; strict concavity and equality in vector triangle give precisely a common partial isometry for p<2. The diagonal-input map has ℓ2-to-S2 norm at most one and ℓ∞-to-operator norm at most sqrt(m), so complex interpolation proves the entire higher range. Positive inputs and the explicit common-output/orthogonal-right family attain all constants. Finite numeric stress tests support, but cannot replace, these arguments.

value.rationale: Commuting moduli are the natural maximal simultaneous-spectral subclass of the active Lee-type matrix-modulus problem, not an arbitrary finite slice. The complete sharp all-m/all-p phase diagram has a Hilbertian transition; the lower-half rigid equality classification explains how a common left polar factor becomes forced while a different geometrically extremal pattern governs upper-half sharpness. General matrix sums lack this coefficient-one lower-half property, so the theorem identifies a structural mechanism genuinely absent in unrestricted estimates.
